import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/titanic.csv')

# Create an insightful visualization: Survival Rate by Passenger Class and Sex
# Using seaborn.catplot with kind='bar' to show the mean survival rate for each group.
# The 'class' column provides more descriptive labels ('First', 'Second', 'Third') than 'pclass'.
g = sns.catplot(
    data=df,
    x='class',       # Passenger class as categorical groups on the x-axis
    y='survived',    # Survival status (will be aggregated to mean survival rate)
    hue='sex',       # Differentiate bars by 'sex' (male/female)
    kind='bar',      # Bar plot to show mean and confidence interval
    palette='viridis', # Color palette for the bars
    height=6,        # Height of the plot
    aspect=1.5       # Aspect ratio of the plot
)

# Set the main title for the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle("Survival Rate on Titanic by Passenger Class and Sex", y=1.02, fontsize=16)

# Set axis labels
g.set_axis_labels("Passenger Class", "Survival Rate")

# Adjust legend title for clarity
g._legend.set_title("Sex")

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
